title: How to Find the Right Therapist (and Know When It's Not Working)
description: A practical guide to finding a therapist who's right for you. What to look for, red flags, how to search, and when to switch.

content.text: Finding the right therapist can feel overwhelming. There are dozens of therapy types, various credentials, and the pressure of knowing you'll be sharing personal details with a stranger. Here's how to navigate it.

items: Psychiatrist (MD/DO): Can prescribe medication, may or may not do therapy
Psychologist (PhD/PsyD): Doctoral-level training, can do testing
LCSW (Licensed Clinical Social Worker): Master's level, common and effective
LMFT (Marriage & Family Therapist): Specializes in relationships

content.text: Research shows the therapeutic relationship matters more than the therapist's specific degree. Focus on fit and approach over credentials.

items: Therapist matching services (Alma, Headway, Grow Therapy)
Ask your primary care doctor for referrals
What's your experience with [your specific issue]?
What does a typical session look like?
What's your availability and cancellation policy?
How do you handle crises between sessions?
Makes you feel judged or dismissed
Pushes you faster than you're comfortable
No clear treatment plan after several sessions
You've given it 4-6 sessions and don't feel any connection
Your therapist doesn't seem to remember key details
You've raised concerns and nothing changed
Your needs have evolved beyond their expertise

content.text: The 'right' therapist is one you feel comfortable with who has experience with your concerns. It's okay to shop around. The relationship is the foundation—skills can be learned, but connection can't be forced.
